headline: US Special Envoy Sergio Gor says US investors to visit Bangladesh next week
summary: The US envoy met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to discuss bilateral ties and potential investment opportunities in the country.
details: US Special Envoy Sergio Gor met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's Office on Saturday morning.
Following the meeting, Gor stated that the discussion was productive and that a group of US investors would visit Bangladesh next week.
The visiting investors plan to conduct feasibility studies to identify specific sectors where US companies can invest in Bangladesh.
The two leaders also discussed ways to strengthen bilateral relations between the United States and Bangladesh.
Prior to the meeting, Sergio Gor visited Rohingya refugee camps in Ukhiya and Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, on Friday.
During his visit to the camps, he observed the overall situation, humanitarian aid activities, and the living conditions of the displaced Rohingya people.
He also held discussions with government officials, international organizations, and representatives involved in humanitarian aid efforts.
The envoy arrived in Dhaka on July 30 for a three-day official visit, which is seen as part of the ongoing dialogue between the two nations.
caption:
US investors are heading to Bangladesh! 🇺🇸🇧🇩

US Special Envoy Sergio Gor met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Prime Minister's Office on Saturday morning.

Following the meeting, Gor stated that the discussion was productive and that a group of US investors would visit Bangladesh next week.

The visiting investors plan to conduct feasibility studies to identify specific sectors where US companies can invest in Bangladesh.

The two leaders also discussed ways to strengthen bilateral relations between the United States and Bangladesh.

Prior to the meeting, Sergio Gor visited Rohingya refugee camps in Ukhiya and Teknaf, Cox's Bazar, on Friday.

During his visit to the camps, he observed the overall situation, humanitarian aid activities, and the living conditions of the displaced Rohingya people.

He also held discussions with government officials, international organizations, and representatives involved in humanitarian aid efforts.

The envoy arrived in Dhaka on July 30 for a three-day official visit, which is seen as part of the ongoing dialogue between the two nations.

headline_marked: US [[urges global partners to increase contributions]] for Rohingya camps
headline: US urges global partners to increase contributions for Rohingya camps
summary: US Special Envoy Sergio Gor visited the world's largest refugee camp in Ukhiya, calling for more international support for over one million displaced people.
details: US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor led a 14-member high-level delegation to the Rohingya camps in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, where he urged international partners to increase their contributions to support the displaced population.

During the visit to Camp-4, the delegation observed the humanitarian assistance operations of the World Food Programme (WFP) and met with refugees, highlighting the scale of the largest refugee camp in the world, which hosts over one million people.
Beyond the humanitarian crisis, US Special Envoy Gor met with Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman to discuss strengthening the US-Bangladesh relationship and positive developments in bilateral ties.
In a significant diplomatic shift, the US State Department has downgraded its travel advisory for Bangladesh from Level 3 (Reconsider Travel) to Level 2 (Exercise Increased Caution).

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) stated that this improvement reflects growing US confidence in Bangladesh's overall security environment and stability under the current government's efforts to improve law and order.

The Bangladeshi government views this travel advisory downgrade as recognition of the sustained efforts to ensure security, stability, and an enabling environment for international travel, trade, and investment.

The US has called for more global support for over one million Rohingyas in Cox's Bazar while simultaneously downgrading its travel advisory for Bangladesh.

US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor led a 14-member high-level delegation to the Rohingya camps in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, where he urged international partners to increase their contributions to support the displaced population.

During the visit to Camp-4, the delegation observed the humanitarian assistance operations of the World Food Programme (WFP) and met with refugees, highlighting the scale of the largest refugee camp in the world, which hosts over one million people.

Beyond the humanitarian crisis, US Special Envoy Gor met with Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman to discuss strengthening the US-Bangladesh relationship and positive developments in bilateral ties.

In a significant diplomatic shift, the US State Department has downgraded its travel advisory for Bangladesh from Level 3 (Reconsider Travel) to Level 2 (Exercise Increased Caution).

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) stated that this improvement reflects growing US confidence in Bangladesh's overall security environment and stability under the current government's efforts to improve law and order.

The Bangladeshi government views this travel advisory downgrade as recognition of the sustained efforts to ensure security, stability, and an enabling environment for international travel, trade, and investment.
